# Kali Linux Tutorials – EINITIAL24 Academy

> A free, chapter-by-chapter Kali Linux course. This site adds written lesson notes, practical
> checklists and official documentation links to the original YouTube playlist. Video content
> belongs to EINITIAL24 ACADEMY and is linked, never re-hosted.

- Canonical site: https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/
- Source repository: https://github.com/bevijaygupta/kali-linux-tutorial
- YouTube playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLYDHfwsEk0RY
- Channel: https://www.youtube.com/@EINITIAL24
- Chapters: 76 (0 published, 28 scheduled)
- Metadata last checked: 2026-11-16

## How to use this site

- Start with the [study roadmap](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/study-roadmap/).
- Set up an isolated lab using the [lab checklist](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/resources/lab-checklist/).
- Follow lessons in chapter order; the YouTube playlist is newest-first.
- Practice only on systems you own or have explicit written permission to test.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/getting-started/): How to use the course, prerequisites and the fastest path to your first lab.
- [Installation](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/installation/): Download Kali Linux safely, verify the ISO and install it in a virtual machine.
- [Lab setup](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/lab-setup/): Build an isolated, snapshot-backed lab for legal practice.
- [Linux fundamentals](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/linux-fundamentals/): Terminal basics, files, permissions, users and processes.
- [Networking basics](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/networking-basics/): IP addresses, ports, DNS, HTTP and how traffic moves.
- [Reconnaissance](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/reconnaissance/): Footprinting, OSINT, DNS enumeration and Nmap scanning.
- [Vulnerability analysis](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/vulnerability-analysis/): Searchsploit, Nikto, Lynis and reading scan results.
- [Exploitation basics](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/exploitation-basics/): Metasploit concepts and safe exploitation in a lab.
- [Password attacks](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/password-attacks/): Hashing, wordlists, offline cracking and online attacks.
- [Wireless security](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/wireless-security/): Wi-Fi security concepts, Aircrack-ng and defending your network.
- [Web application security](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/web-application-security/): XSS, SQL injection, Burp Suite and Wireshark.
- [Study roadmap](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/docs/study-roadmap/): A week-by-week plan for finishing the course.

## Resources

- [Cheat sheet](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/resources/cheat-sheet/): Safe command reference for the tools covered in the course.
- [Lab checklist](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/resources/lab-checklist/): Pre-flight checks before every practice session.
- [Official links](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/resources/official-links/): Vendor and project documentation, plus acceptable use rules.
- [Glossary](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/resources/glossary/): Plain-language definitions of course terminology.

## Lessons

- [Chapter 1: Why Use Kali Linux? Kali vs Ubuntu for Ethical Hacking](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-001/): Learn what Kali Linux is, where it came from, how it differs from Ubuntu, and who should use it. Chapter 1 of the free Kali Linux course by EINITIAL24. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 2: Linux Is NOT Unix? Unix vs Linux Explained for Beginners](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-002/): Unix vs Linux explained for beginners: history, licensing, technical differences, and where Kali Linux fits. Chapter 2 of the EINITIAL24 Kali course. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 3: How to Download Kali Linux Safely (Avoid Fake ISOs)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-003/): Download Kali Linux safely from the official site, choose the right image type, and verify the SHA256 checksum. Chapter 3 of the free Kali Linux tutorial series. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 4: How to Install VirtualBox (Windows, Mac, Linux) + Best Settings](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-004/): Set up VirtualBox for Kali Linux: installation on Windows, macOS and Linux, Extension Pack, RAM and CPU settings, plus NAT vs Bridged vs Host-Only networking. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 5: Linux Terminal for Beginners: Don't Be Afraid of It](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-005/): Learn the Linux terminal from scratch: terminal vs shell vs command line, reading the prompt, navigating Kali Linux, and beginner shortcuts that save time. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 6: 22 Essential Linux Commands for Beginners (Kali Linux)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-006/): Learn 22 essential Linux commands for Kali Linux: navigation, files, search, permissions and system information, with examples you can run in a safe VM. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 7: Linux ls Command Explained: ls -l, ls -a, ls -lh (Beginners)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-007/): Master the Linux ls command: long listings, hidden files, human-readable sizes and the everyday commands cd, pwd, clear and history. Kali Linux chapter 7. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 8: Linux cd Command Explained: cd .., cd ~, cd - (Beginners)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-008/): Learn the Linux cd command: absolute and relative paths, cd .., cd ~, cd - and touch, with practical examples for Kali Linux beginners. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 9: Linux rm Command: How to Delete Files Safely (rm -rf Explained)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-009/): Understand Linux deletion: mkdir, rm, rmdir, rm -r, rm -f and rm -rf, plus the rm -i safety prompt. Learn why Linux has no recycle bin. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 10: Linux cp Command: How to Copy Files and Folders (cp -r Explained)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-010/): Learn how to copy files and folders in Linux with cp, cp -r and cp -v, then read them with cat, less, head and tail. Beginner-friendly Kali Linux guide. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 11: How to Find Files in Linux Fast: locate, find, updatedb](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-011/): Learn how to find files in Linux with locate and find, refresh the database with updatedb, and move or rename files with mv. Kali Linux chapter 11. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 12: Linux sort Command Explained: sort -n, -r, -k, -u (Beginners)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-012/): Fix the classic '10 before 2' problem and learn Linux sort: numeric sorting with -n, reverse with -r, columns with -k, duplicates with -u and pipes. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 13: How to Zip and Unzip Files in Linux (zip -r, unzip -d)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-013/): Create and extract archives in Linux: zip, zip -r, unzip, unzip -l and unzip -d, plus installing zip and unzip on Kali Linux. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 14: Linux history Command: View, Reuse and Clear (+ whereis)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-014/): Learn Linux command history: view past commands, reuse them with !! and !n, clear with history -c, and locate programs with whereis and which. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 15: How to Create a User in Linux: adduser, passwd, su Explained](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-015/): Create and manage Linux users: adduser vs useradd, passwd, su vs su -, and why sudo and least privilege matter. Chapter 15 of the Kali Linux course. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 16: chmod Explained: Linux File Permissions (755, 777, +x)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-016/): Understand Linux file permissions and chmod: read the ls -l string, calculate 755 and 644, use symbolic modes, make scripts executable and avoid chmod 777. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 17: chmod u+x, g-w, o=r Explained: Symbolic Permissions in Linux](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-017/): Read permission strings like -rwxr-xr-- and change them with chmod u+x, g-w, o=r, = and combined symbolic modes. Clear examples for Kali Linux beginners. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 18: Permission Denied in Linux? How to Fix File & Folder Permissions](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-018/): Fix 'permission denied' in Linux with practical chmod examples: executable scripts, restricted files, recursive changes and group-shared folders. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 19: Linux Terminal Shortcuts: Ctrl+R, Ctrl+C, Tab and More (Beginners)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-019/): Speed up Linux terminal work with Tab completion, Ctrl+R history search, line editing shortcuts, Ctrl+C and command repetition. Beginner-friendly guide. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 20: Is Kali Linux Anonymous? Tor vs VPN vs Proxy Explained](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-020/): Does Kali Linux make you anonymous? Learn how IP addresses, DNS leaks and browser fingerprints expose you, and how Tor, VPNs and proxies differ. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 21: Proxy Server Explained: How It Hides Your IP (And What It Can't)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-021/): What is a proxy server and how does it hide your IP? Compare HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS proxies, forward vs reverse proxies, and the limits of proxy anonymity. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 22: AnonSurf on Kali Linux: Route Your Traffic Through Tor (Setup)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-022/): Install and use AnonSurf on Kali Linux: git clone, read the installer, start and stop Tor routing, and verify your public IP actually changed. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 23: What Is a VPN? How It Works vs Proxy vs Tor (Beginners)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-023/): Learn how a VPN works: the encrypted tunnel, how websites see the VPN server's IP, OpenVPN vs WireGuard vs IPsec, and what a VPN cannot protect. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 24: How to Use OpenVPN on Kali Linux (.ovpn Setup, Step by Step)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-024/): Connect Kali Linux to a VPN with OpenVPN: install the client, inspect a .ovpn profile, connect, verify your IP and DNS, disconnect safely and fix errors. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 25: Is the Dark Web Illegal? How Tor Really Works (Beginners)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-025/): Understand Tor without the myths: surface web vs deep web vs dark web, onion routing, .onion services, and the legal and safety facts beginners need. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 26: How to Host a .onion Website on Tor (XAMPP + Kali Linux Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-026/): Host a harmless .onion test site in a lab: install XAMPP, run Apache, configure a Tor hidden service, find the address and test it in Tor Browser. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 27: How Tor Works: Why No One Can See Both Who You Are and Where You Go](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-027/): A plain-language explanation of onion routing: how Tor wraps traffic in layers, what entry, middle and exit relays can see, and where Tor's limits are. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 28: Proxychains in Kali Linux: Route Any Tool Through Tor (Setup)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-028/): Configure Proxychains to send tool traffic through Tor: edit proxychains4.conf, choose a chain mode, test the circuit, and understand Nmap limitations. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 29: Tor + Proxychains in Kali Linux: Do It Right (Step by Step)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-029/): Combine Tor and Proxychains correctly: start services in order, verify traffic uses an exit node, avoid silent bypasses and troubleshoot common failures. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 30: Change Your MAC Address in Kali Linux (macchanger Tutorial)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-030/): Learn MAC address spoofing in Kali Linux with macchanger: what a MAC address is, random and custom addresses, restoring the original, and legal limits. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 31: Macchanger Commands Explained: Every Option in Kali Linux](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-031/): A complete macchanger reference for Kali Linux: show, random, same-vendor, custom, restore and troubleshoot the interface-is-up error. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 32: What Is Footprinting? First Step of Ethical Hacking Explained](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-032/): Footprinting explained: passive vs active reconnaissance, what information is collected, where it comes from, and how it feeds scanning and enumeration. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 33: DNS Enumeration in Kali Linux: dig, nslookup & dnsenum](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-033/): Learn DNS enumeration with dig and nslookup: read A, AAAA, MX, NS and TXT records, map a domain's infrastructure and understand reconnaissance scope. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 34: Dnsenum Tutorial: Find Subdomains Automatically in Kali Linux](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-034/): Use Dnsenum in Kali Linux to automate DNS enumeration: run it against an authorized domain, read the output, and find subdomains with wordlists. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 35: DNSmap Tutorial: Find Subdomains with Wordlists in Kali Linux](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-035/): Learn DNSmap in Kali Linux: wordlist-driven subdomain discovery, custom wordlists, reading results, and how it differs from Dnsenum. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 36: DNStracer Tutorial: Trace DNS Resolution in Kali Linux](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-036/): Trace DNS resolution with DNStracer: follow a query from root to TLD to authoritative servers, read the delegation path, and use it during recon. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 37: Nmap for Beginners: Check Your Network First (ifconfig, route -n)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-037/): Before scanning with Nmap, learn your own network: ip a and ifconfig for addresses, route -n for the gateway, then a safe first host-discovery scan in your lab. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 38: Nmap Scan Types Explained: -sS vs -sT vs -sU (Kali Linux Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-038/): Learn Nmap scanning: basic syntax, host ranges, -sS vs -sT vs -sU, port selection, -sV service detection, -O OS detection and saving output. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 39: Nmap Scans Explained: ACK, FIN, Xmas, -A and NSE (Kali Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-039/): Go deeper with Nmap: ACK, FIN and Xmas scans, -T0 to -T5 timing, the -A aggressive scan, output formats -oN -oX -oG -oA, and NSE basics. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 40: Searchsploit Tutorial: Find Exploits for Nmap Results (Kali Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-040/): Use Searchsploit to turn Nmap service versions into vulnerability research: search Exploit-DB, filter results, inspect entries, update the database and stay legal. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 41: WhatWeb, Whois and Dirb in Kali Linux: Recon a Website (Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-041/): Profile a website before testing: WhatWeb technology fingerprinting, Whois domain details and Dirb content discovery, with responsible-use guidance. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 42: Nikto Tutorial: Scan a Web Server for Vulnerabilities (Kali Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-042/): Learn Nikto web server scanning: how vulnerability analysis differs from exploitation, port and SSL options, reading results and prioritising real findings. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 43: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) for Beginners: How It Works and How to Stop It](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-043/): Understand XSS: reflected, stored and DOM-based cross-site scripting, real impact, safe lab testing, and how developers prevent it with encoding and CSP. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 44: RedHawk Tutorial: All-in-One Website Recon Tool (Kali Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-044/): Use RedHawk for website reconnaissance: install with git clone, review the source, run server, Whois, geo-IP and CMS checks, and compare it with dedicated tools. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 45: Linux Security Audit with Lynis: Find Weak Spots in Your System](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-045/): Audit your Linux system: review users, sudo, permissions, services, ports and updates, then run Lynis and interpret the report to prioritise hardening. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 46: SQLMap Tutorial: Test SQL Injection in a Safe Lab (DVWA + Kali)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-046/): Learn SQL injection with SQLMap in a DVWA lab: how detection works, reading output, enumerating databases, real-world impact and developer defences. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 47: jSQL Injection Tutorial: SQL Injection with a GUI (Safe Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-047/): Use jSQL Injection to test SQL injection visually: interface tour, database and table enumeration, data extraction in a lab, and how it compares with SQLMap. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 48: sqlsus Tutorial: MySQL Injection Tool in Kali Linux (Safe Lab)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-048/): Explore sqlsus, a MySQL-focused SQL injection tool: configuration, interactive shell, data extraction, and how it compares with SQLMap and jSQL Injection. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 49: What is a Password Attack? Types Explained](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-049/): Learn password attack types: brute force, dictionary, rainbow table and credential stuffing, online vs offline attacks, hashing and why wordlists matter. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 50: What is Hashing? Explained for Beginners](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-050/): Hashing explained: how hashes differ from encryption, MD5 vs SHA-1 vs SHA-256 vs bcrypt, why passwords are hashed, rainbow tables, brute force and salting. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 51: Hash-Identifier Tutorial: Find Out What Hash Type You Have](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-051/): Use Hash-Identifier to identify MD5, SHA and bcrypt hashes: why format matters, how to read candidate results, and how the type selects your cracking method. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 52: Password & Hash Cracking Tutorial (Hands-On)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-052/): Follow the complete password cracking workflow: choose a wordlist, crack a lab hash, read output, verify the result and troubleshoot failed attempts. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 53: CEWL Tutorial: Build Custom Wordlists from Websites](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-053/): Build targeted wordlists with CEWL: crawl a site, set depth and minimum length, collect metadata, save the list and use it with John or Hydra. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 54: Crunch Tutorial: Generate Wordlists with Custom Patterns](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-054/): Generate wordlists with Crunch: length ranges, custom character sets, pattern-based generation, size estimation and when to use it instead of CEWL. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 55: How to Crack Passwords Offline Using John the Ripper](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-055/): Learn John the Ripper: wordlist, single and incremental modes, --show, and cracking ZIP archive hashes with zip2john in an isolated lab. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 56: How to Extract & Crack SAM and Shadow File Hashes](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-056/): Understand Windows SAM and Linux /etc/shadow, extract hashes with authorization, combine passwd and shadow with unshadow, and crack lab credentials with John. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 57: How to Crack RAR & ZIP File Passwords](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-057/): Recover archive passwords in a lab: extract hashes with zip2john, rar2john and pdf2john, crack them with John and a wordlist, and choose better wordlists. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 58: THC Hydra Tutorial for Beginners (Online Password Attacks)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-058/): Learn THC Hydra: online vs offline attacks, SSH and web form syntax, wordlists, reading results, and why lockouts make online guessing different. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 59: Medusa Tutorial: Online Password Brute Forcing](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-059/): Use Medusa for online password testing: syntax, SSH and FTP modules, parallel testing trade-offs, and how it compares with THC Hydra. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 60: What is Sniffing and Spoofing in Ethical Hacking?](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-060/): Sniffing and spoofing explained: passive vs active capture, ARP, IP, MAC and DNS spoofing, why unencrypted traffic is vulnerable, and the tools used next. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 61: How to Use Wireshark for Network Sniffing](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-061/): Wireshark for beginners: choose an interface, capture traffic, navigate packet panes, use display filters, follow TCP streams and save evidence. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 62: How to Capture Network Packets Using Wireshark (Practical Guide)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-062/): Capture packets efficiently with Wireshark: capture vs display filters, wired and wireless interfaces, HTTP traffic, login analysis, and saving pcap files. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 63: How Wireshark Captures Packets From Another Machine (Remote Sniffing Explained)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-063/): How analysts capture traffic from another machine: SPAN ports, ARP spoofing and MITM concepts, SSH remote capture with tcpdump, and legal authorization. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 64: What Is a Spoofing Attack? ARP, DNS & IP Spoofing Explained](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-064/): Learn how spoofing works: ARP cache poisoning, IP source forgery, DNS spoofing and MAC spoofing, plus the defences that detect or prevent each attack. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 65: DNS Spoofing Attack Explained & Demonstrated](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-065/): DNS spoofing explained: how forged answers redirect victims, a lab demonstration with Ettercap and dnsspoof, combined ARP MITM, impact and defences. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 66: How to Configure Ettercap on Kali Linux (Step-by-Step Setup)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-066/): Configure Ettercap for lab work: GUI vs console mode, interface selection, etter.conf settings, DNS spoof plugin, etter.dns and common errors. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 67: WiFi Hacking Basics: Important Terms Explained Before You Start](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-067/): Wireless security terms explained: SSID vs BSSID, access points, channels, WEP to WPA3, the four-way handshake, monitor mode, injection and PMKID. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 68: How to Hack WEP WiFi Networks Using Aircrack-ng (Step-by-Step)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-068/): Learn the WEP attack workflow in a lab: monitor mode with airmon-ng, capture with airodump-ng, injection with aireplay-ng, and cracking with aircrack-ng. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 69: How to Crack WPA/WPA2 WiFi Passwords Using Aircrack-ng](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-069/): WPA2 handshake capture and offline cracking in a lab: airodump-ng, deauth, verifying the handshake, aircrack-ng with a wordlist and passphrase defence. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 70: Fern WiFi Cracker Tutorial — GUI-Based WEP/WPA2 Attacks](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-070/): Use Fern WiFi Cracker in a lab: interface selection, monitor mode, network scanning, automated WEP and WPA/WPA2 tests, and GUI vs Aircrack-ng trade-offs. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 71: What Is Metasploit? Beginner's Guide to the Metasploit Framework](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-071/): Metasploit for beginners: exploits, payloads, auxiliary and post modules, msfconsole navigation, search, show options and setting targets safely in a lab. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 72: How to Exploit a Buffer Overflow Vulnerability with Metasploit](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-072/): Understand buffer overflows and run a Metasploit exploit in an isolated lab: Nmap service discovery, module configuration, payloads, sessions and mitigations. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 73: Honeypots Explained — How Security Teams Trap Attackers](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-073/): What is a honeypot? Low- vs high-interaction designs, honeypot types, why organizations deploy them, monitoring attacker activity, and legal containment. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 74: Pentbox Tutorial — Setting Up a Honeypot with Pentbox](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-074/): Set up a Pentbox honeypot in an isolated lab: install Ruby dependencies, navigate the menu, configure logging, test connections and review captured activity. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 75: Browser Exploitation Attack Using Metasploit (BeEF Framework Demo)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-075/): Learn browser exploitation in a lab: BeEF setup and browser hooking, Metasploit browser modules, payload delivery, and the defences that stop this attack class. (scheduled)
- [Chapter 76: How to Perform an Attack Using BeEF (Hooked Browser Modules Explained)](https://bevijaygupta.github.io/kali-linux-tutorial/lessons/lesson-076/): Explore BeEF command modules: social engineering, browser information gathering, persistence, chaining with Metasploit, and defences like CSP and script blockers. (scheduled)
